mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening consumer demand and construction activity, which typically precedes higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is rising (defined as 3-month growth > 0.5%)

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 0.5% and is rising, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and rising (3-month change > 0.1%)

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in non-farm payrolls signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS up and UNRATE down) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the correlation between the joint signal and returns is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of industrial production contraction (INDPRO < 105.0), the S&P 500 tends to decline in the following 60 days as manufacturing weakness signals an impending recession.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO < 105.0, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising CPIAUCSL (inflation) indicates increasing price pressures that may lead to central bank tightening, which typically depresses equity valuations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL is rising (3-month change > 0.2%)

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 2.5% on a year-over-year basis, it signals a strong economy that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 YoY growth > 2.5%

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS (policy rate) signals a monetary tightening cycle in response to inflation, which typically causes a sell-off in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (CPIAUCSL rising and FEDFUNDS rising) fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the correlation is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%), the S&P 500 tends to rise in the following 20 days as labor market tightness supports consumer spending and corporate margins.
failure_condition: In periods when UNRATE < 4.5%, the S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).
